newsitem.title: UK: Cold snap boosts NWE high sulphur fuel,market slow.
newsitem.headline: Cold snap boosts NWE high sulphur fuel,market slow.

text.p: The cold snap gripping much of Europe was giving support to fuel oil on Thursday, but activity was still muted after the holiday season.
"Prices look a touch firmer, but I've not seen anyone doing anything at the moment," said one trader at a major.
"I'm not sure whether its because people are covered or whether they are still on holiday," said another dealer.

High sulphur cracked barges rose sharply with $118 and $119 fob ARA a tonne done. Cargoes were also pegged higher. "People are talking about competing with barge numbers for prompt material and $116-117 cif NWE for mid Jan," said one end-user.
A Scandinavian cargo was understood to be loading Jan 8-10 with talk centred on floating rather than fixed prices.
The low sulphur cracked market was steady around $125 fob NWE. A 20kt cargo loading promptly was expected to be sold today or tomorrow, but business was slow.
"You would think prices would go up (with the cold and futures) but there is no real evidence of that. There's plenty of oil, but no buying out there," said a trader at a major.
Dealers said there was little opportunity for barrels to move to the U.S since natural gas prices have weakened in the east coast. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8980
